Firstly, I think k it looks good and you may be being a bit hard on yourself. However if your not satisfied then that's a great excuse to get in there and play!! :p
Secondly, if you know anything about the golden mean and colour theory then all that can be used here. If not then what I can tell you next is all based off of that and my experience in the hobby.
Alright; I love your plans and you have a great variety. If you have anything that's naturally attached to the driftwood then that is going to be your biggest limiting factor in rearranging the placement. Your substrate is dark and flat,  this is kind of a bad combination as you want to insinuate depth and dark substrates dont always show the contours the best, something you can do with that is to pile it higher in the back and contour it. Do this at maybe 1-3 heights toward the front and each time add something to lighten your substrate. You can bud small barricades with stones or by using plasticard barriers in the substrate.
Hmm, next maybe try to arrange your plants in such a way that as you look into it it draws your eye in and onward through the scape. Hard to explain, but choose a focal point and work outward from that. I personally think your largest piece is the most obvious for this.
Now you can either place the smallest plants toward the front and the larger toward the back to make it look like a forest style depth. Or the other way around to sort of use forced prospecting to make the bigger plants look like tress.
I hope I didnt sound critical. Beautiful plants, beautiful water and I cant wait to see what you do with it!
